findings.summary: A6/M4 blocker from the prior Final review is resolved. test/cas.test.ts now counts entity reads, serves a *different* head (message_id "msg_003") on any second /entities/ read, and asserts both entityReads === 1 and body.supersedes === "msg_001". An implementation that supersedes on a second independent read now fails on two independent assertions, so M4 is killed and the mutual-exclusion invariant is genuinely falsifiable.

A1/M1 major from the prior Final review is resolved. The new case stubs a genuine HTTP 422 whose body text contains "409" and asserts invalid_payload. busFetch (src/bus.ts:33-42) folds the body into err.message, so a reverted msg.includes("409") implementation would return conflict and fail this assertion. M1 now has a killing assertion; the mechanical grep for includes("4xx") in src/bus.ts is also zero-hit.

The tsx major from the prior Final review is resolved: package.json no longer references tsx (no occurrence anywhere in the product tree or lockfile), and smoke:cas now runs via the already-frozen vitest toolchain. Because scripts/smoke-cas.ts does not match vitest's default test include, it cannot be swept into `npm test`; it runs only under the explicit --config override, satisfying the spec §5 prohibition on wiring the smoke into acceptance.

Both smoke minors are resolved: step ③ now asserts second.error === "conflict" explicitly (not merely !success), and the idempotency keys are fixed deterministic constants, so an accidental re-run dedupes bus-side. Worst-case write volume is 2 messages (step ③ conflicts at the precondition check before any publish), within the hard cap of 3.

Scope observation, not a defect: vitest.smoke.config.ts is a new repository-root file that does not appear in the spec §3 allowed-change table. It is the minimal mechanism for discharging the §5 gate obligation under the frozen dependency set (a bare positional filter cannot select a file outside vitest's include patterns), and it touches neither frozen artifact — src/protocol.ts is byte-identical in substance and test/protocol.test.ts still carries all 11 original cases (A7).

A8 (`npm test` exit 0) was assessed by static reading only; this reviewer has read-only file inspection and executed nothing. Each of the 23 cases (11 protocol + 7 cas + 5 bus) was traced against src/bus.ts control flow and the fetch stub semantics and is consistent; M1→bus A1, M2→A3 (both files), M3→A4 (both files), and M4→A6 each have at least one assertion that flips. Actual execution remains a gate obligation.
